report.feature: Voice & Video Calls — Hangup / Call End
report.title: TypeError: _activeCall_startedAt.getTime is not a function — crash on call hangup
report.symptom: After hanging up a voice or video call, the app throws a TypeError: _activeCall_startedAt.getTime is not a function. This crashes the call teardown logic, likely preventing call_history from being updated with the correct duration and status.

observed_behavior.error: TypeError: _activeCall_startedAt.getTime is not a function. (In '_activeCall_startedAt.getTime()', '_activeCall_startedAt.getTime' is undefined)
observed_behavior.trigger: User clicks the hang-up / end-call button
observed_behavior.consequence: Call teardown logic crashes mid-execution — call_history row may not be updated to status='completed', duration_seconds may remain null, call_ended Ably event may not be published to the other participant

root_cause.summary: startedAt is being used as a JavaScript Date object (calling .getTime()) but the value is either a raw ISO string returned from the database/API (e.g. '2026-03-02T10:01:03.686Z'), null, or undefined. Drizzle ORM returns timestamptz columns as strings by default in some configurations, and JSON serialization over the API always converts Date objects to ISO strings. The code that computes duration_seconds does: Math.floor((endedAt.getTime() - startedAt.getTime()) / 1000) — which breaks if either value is not a proper Date instance.

affected_locations.description: startedAt read from call_history row is an ISO string or null, not a Date object

affected_locations.location: hooks/useCallState.ts or hooks/useLiveKitRoom.ts — client-side duration display
affected_locations.description: activeCall.startedAt stored in state/context may be an ISO string received from the API response, not a Date

affected_locations.location: components/calls/CallControls.tsx or call room page — elapsed timer
affected_locations.description: UI timer that shows call duration may call .getTime() on the raw string value

bugs.title: startedAt not coerced to Date before .getTime() call in hangup handler
startedAt can be null if callee never fully joined — duration computation not null-guarded
error_messages: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getTime')

agent_prompt.role: You are a senior full-stack engineer working on TruckConnect, a Next.js 14 App Router application. Fix a TypeError crash that occurs when a user hangs up a voice or video call. The error is: TypeError: _activeCall_startedAt.getTime is not a function.
agent_prompt.objective: Ensure that every place in the codebase that reads startedAt or endedAt from the call_history table or from API responses safely coerces the value to a Date object before calling any Date methods, and that null/undefined values are fully guarded.

fix_A.title: Fix duration_seconds computation in DELETE /api/calls/[roomName]/route.ts
instructions: Open app/api/calls/[roomName]/route.ts and find the DELETE handler
Locate where duration_seconds is computed — it will look like: Math.floor((endedAt.getTime() - call.startedAt.getTime()) / 1000) or similar
The value returned by Drizzle for a timestamptz column is a string in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2026-03-02T10:01:03.686Z') — it is NOT automatically a Date object
Replace all raw .getTime() calls with a safe helper that coerces the value first
Create a toDate helper inline or import from lib/utils.ts: const toDate = (v: Date | string | null | undefined): Date | null => { if (!v) return null; return v instanceof Date ? v : new Date(v); }

Use the helper to safely compute duration: const startedAt = toDate(call.startedAt); const endedAt = new Date(); const durationSeconds = startedAt ? Math.floor((endedAt.getTime() - startedAt.getTime()) / 1000) : null;
Update the Drizzle update call to set: { status: 'completed', endedAt: endedAt, durationSeconds: durationSeconds }
Never pass null to durationSeconds if it is defined as NOT NULL in the schema — if startedAt is null, set durationSeconds to 0 as a safe fallback

fix_B.title: Fix client-side activeCall.startedAt usage in useCallState and UI components
instructions: Search the entire codebase for every occurrence of .getTime() — run: grep -rn '.getTime()' hooks/ components/ app/ to find all call sites
For every occurrence that operates on startedAt, endedAt, or any timestamp received from an API response or Drizzle query result, wrap it with the safe coercion pattern

In hooks/useCallState.ts: when storing activeCall in state, ensure startedAt is stored as a Date object, not a string. If the value comes from an API response, coerce it on receipt: startedAt: data.startedAt ? new Date(data.startedAt) : null

The ActiveCallBadge component likely shows an elapsed timer using setInterval — find where it computes elapsed seconds and ensure it does: const start = activeCall.startedAt instanceof Date ? activeCall.startedAt : new Date(activeCall.startedAt ?? Date.now()); const elapsed = Math.floor((Date.now() - start.getTime()) / 1000);

Add a shared utility function toDate to lib/utils.ts so it can be reused everywhere: export const toDate = (v: Date | string | null | undefined): Date | null => { if (v == null) return null; return v instanceof Date ? v : new Date(v); };
Replace all inline coercions with the imported toDate utility for consistency

In the call room page or useLiveKitRoom hook, if the call start time is set when the room connects, use: const startedAt = new Date(); — always create a fresh Date object, never rely on a value received as a string without coercion

fix_C.title: Add null-safety guard to the PATCH /api/calls/[roomName]/decline route
instructions: Open the decline route handler
When a call is declined, startedAt will always be null (the call was never answered)
Ensure the handler does NOT attempt to compute duration_seconds when startedAt is null
Set durationSeconds: 0 and status: 'declined' directly without any date arithmetic
This prevents a secondary crash if the decline route accidentally tries to compute a duration

verification_steps.action: Run: grep -rn '\.getTime()' hooks/ components/ app/ -- review every result and confirm each one is preceded by a toDate() coercion or instanceof Date check
Initiate a voice call, let it connect, then hang up — verify NO TypeError in the console and the call ends cleanly
Initiate a video call and immediately hang up before the callee answers — verify durationSeconds is set to 0, not null, and no crash occurs
Decline an incoming call — verify no crash and call_history row shows status='declined', durationSeconds=0
Let a call run for 30 seconds then hang up — verify the call_ended Ably event is received by the other participant and the ActiveCallBadge shows the correct elapsed time before dismissing
Query the call_history table directly (npm run db:studio) after each scenario and confirm endedAt, durationSeconds, and status are all correctly set

constraints: Do not change the Drizzle schema column type — handle the string-to-Date coercion in application code, not at the ORM layer
The toDate utility must handle all four input types: Date, string, null, and undefined — it must never throw
durationSeconds must never be stored as null if the column is NOT NULL — use 0 as the safe fallback for unanswered/declined calls
Do not use any external date library (e.g. date-fns, dayjs, moment) — the native Date constructor is sufficient for this fix
All existing call flow logic (Ably events, LiveKit room deletion) must still execute after the duration fix — the fix must not short-circuit the rest of the DELETE handler
